source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Note the date and time of the inspection.
3. Document the exact name and location of the building.
4. Record the accessibility standards being enforced (e.g., ADA, AODA).

5. Identify the inspector’s name and contact information.
6. List the specific areas or features checked.
7. Detail each failed accessibility check:

- Describe the issue (e.g., inadequate ramp width, missing audible bathroom signals).
- Provide precise measurements and details for quantitative issues (e.g., ADA requires a ramp slope of no more than 1:12; measured slope is 1:10).
- Include photographic or pictorial evidence (ensure the photos are dated and labeled).
- Explain why the feature fails to comply with the accessibility standards.

8. Cite the specific section of the accessibility standards the building does not comply with (e.g., ADA Title III, Section 36.302(d)).
9. Document any attempts to communicate with the building owner
